chapters.title: Saul's Sacrifice at Gilgal
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 13

Jonathan Strikes the Garrison

1Saul was [number lost] years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years over Israel.

2Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, each to his tent.

3Jonathan struck down the Philistine garrison at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the horn throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"

4All Israel heard it said, "Saul has struck down the Philistine garrison, and Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines." The people were called out to follow Saul to Gilgal.

5The Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as many as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

6When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, for the people were hard pressed, the people hid themselves in caves and in thickets, among the rocks, in strongholds and in cisterns.

7Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.

Saul Offers the Burnt Offering

8He waited seven days, to the appointed time that Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.

9So Saul said, "Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings." Then he offered the burnt offering.

10And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Samuel came. Saul went out to meet him and to greet him.

11Samuel said, "What have you done?" Saul said, "When I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come at the appointed days, and that the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,

12I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the LORD's favor.' So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering."

13Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God that He commanded you. For now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

14But now your kingdom shall not stand. The LORD has sought for Himself a man after His own heart, and the LORD has appointed him leader over His people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you."

15Then Samuel arose and went from Gilgal on his way. The rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the fighting men, and they came from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.

No Smith in Israel

16Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were present with them stayed at Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.

17The raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;

18another company turned toward the road to Beth-horon; and another company turned toward the road of the border that looks down on the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.

19No smith was to be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, "In case the Hebrews make a sword or a spear."

20So all Israel went down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe and his sickle.

21The charge was a pim for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and for the three-pronged forks and for the axes, and for setting the goads.

22So on the day of battle neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and Jonathan his son had them.

23The Philistine garrison went out to the pass of Michmash.

Notes

  • v1 "Saul was [number lost] years old when he began to reign" — the Hebrew reads ben shanah Sha'ul be-molkho, a son of a year was Saul when he reigned. This is the formula for a king's age at his accession, as in David was thirty years old when he began to reign (2 Samuel 5:4), and the number that belongs before year is missing from the text. The Greek does not have the verse. Two years is what the Hebrew has for the length of the reign; Paul gives Saul forty years (Acts 13:21).

  • v3 "Let the Hebrews hear!" — Saul calls Israel by the name the Philistines use for them (4:6, 4:9, and v19). The Greek has The slaves have revolted; ha-ivrim, the Hebrews, and ha-avadim, the slaves, differ by one letter.

  • v4 "Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines" — niv'ash, the word of Jacob's rebuke to Simeon and Levi after Shechem, to make me stink among those who dwell in the land (Genesis 34:30). The report gives Saul the credit for Jonathan's blow (v3).

  • vv6–7 "hid themselves in caves… Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan" — ve-ivrim avru: the name Hebrews and the verb crossed share their letters. The Greek has those who crossed over crossed. The people who were called out in v4 hide or flee.

  • v8 "to the appointed time that Samuel had set" — the Hebrew has no verb, the appointed time that Samuel; had set is supplied. The appointment is the one Samuel gave at the anointing: Seven days you shall wait, until I come to you and show you what you are to do (10:8). Saul waits the seven days, and Samuel comes as the offering ends.

  • vv12–13 "I have not sought the LORD's favor… So I forced myself… You have acted foolishly" — u-fenei YHWH lo chilliti, the face of the LORD I have not entreated, the phrase for asking for favor. Va-etappaq is the verb of Joseph who held himself in before his brothers (Genesis 43:31, 45:1): Saul says he acted against his own will. Samuel's answer is niskalta. David uses the same word of himself after the census, I have acted very foolishly (2 Samuel 24:10), and Saul will say I have played the fool to David (26:21).

  • v14 "a man after His own heart… leader over His people" — ish ki-levavo. Paul uses the words of David: I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my heart (Acts 13:22). Nagid, leader, is the word the LORD used of Saul (9:16, 10:1); it is now given to another.

  • v15 "went from Gilgal on his way. The rest of the people went up after Saul… from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin" — these words are in the Greek. The Hebrew has Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin, sending Samuel to Saul's town; from Gilgal stands twice in the Greek, and the Hebrew has passed from the first to the second. The text follows the Greek.

  • v17 "The raiders" — ha-mashchit, the destroyer, the word of the Passover night, He will not let the destroyer come into your houses (Exodus 12:23). Here it is the Philistine raiding force.

Jonathan Strikes the Garrison
Saul was [number lost] years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years over Israel.

Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, each to his tent.
Jonathan struck down the Philistine garrison at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the horn throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
All Israel heard it said, "Saul has struck down the Philistine garrison, and Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines." The people were called out to follow Saul to Gilgal.

The Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people as many as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
When the men of Israel saw that they were in a strait, for the people were hard pressed, the people hid themselves in caves and in thickets, among the rocks, in strongholds and in cisterns.

chapters.title: Jonathan's Victory and Saul's Oath
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 14

Jonathan and His Armor-bearer

1And it came to pass one day that Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let us cross over to the Philistine garrison on the other side." But he did not tell his father.

2Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree at Migron, and the people with him were about six hundred men.

3Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. The people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

4Between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other side. The name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

5The one crag rose on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

6Jonathan said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few."

7His armor-bearer said to him, "Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you, as your heart is."

8Jonathan said, "We will cross over to the men and show ourselves to them.

9If they say to us, 'Wait until we come to you,' then we will stand where we are and not go up to them.

10But if they say, 'Come up to us,' then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand. This will be the sign for us."

11So the two of them showed themselves to the Philistine garrison, and the Philistines said, "See, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves."

12The men of the garrison called to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, "Come up to us, and we will show you something!" Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Come up after me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."

13Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. They fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer killed them behind him.

14That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor-bearer made, was about twenty men, within about half a furrow's length in an acre of field.

15There was trembling in the camp, in the field and among all the people. The garrison and the raiders also trembled. The earth quaked, and it became a trembling from God.

The LORD Saved Israel

16Saul's watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and the multitude was melting away, surging here and there.

17Saul said to the people who were with him, "Count now and see who has gone from us." When they counted, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

18Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ephod here," for he carried the ephod on that day before Israel.

19And it came to pass, while Saul was talking to the priest, that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines went on growing louder. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."

20Saul and all the people who were with him rallied and came to the battle, and every man's sword was against his fellow, in very great confusion.

21The Hebrews who had been with the Philistines before, who had gone up with them into the camp from all around, also turned to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.

22All the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, and they too pursued them closely in the battle.

23So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-aven.

Saul's Oath

24The men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul had put the people under an oath, saying, "Cursed be the man who eats food until evening, until I have taken vengeance on my enemies." So none of the people tasted food.

25All the people of the land came into the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

26When the people came into the forest, the honey was flowing, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

27But Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under the oath. He put out the end of the staff that was in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.

28Then one of the people said, "Your father strictly put the people under oath, saying, 'Cursed be the man who eats food today.'" The people were faint.

29Jonathan said, "My father has brought trouble on the land. See how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

30How much more, if the people had eaten freely today from the spoil of their enemies that they found! For now the slaughter among the Philistines has not been great."

31They struck down the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very faint.

32The people pounced on the spoil and took sheep and cattle and calves and slaughtered them on the ground, and the people ate them with the blood.

33They told Saul, "See, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood." He said, "You have dealt faithlessly. Roll a great stone to me today."

34Saul said, "Scatter among the people and say to them, 'Each of you bring me his ox or his sheep, and slaughter them here and eat, and do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.'" So all the people brought each his ox with him that night and slaughtered them there.

35Saul built an altar to the LORD. It was the first altar he built to the LORD.

Jonathan Taken by Lot

36Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them." They said, "Do whatever seems good in your eyes." But the priest said, "Let us draw near to God here."

37Saul asked God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?" But He did not answer him that day.

38Saul said, "Come here, all you leaders of the people, and find out and see how this sin has come about today.

39For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall die." But not one of all the people answered him.

40He said to all Israel, "You be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side." The people said to Saul, "Do what seems good in your eyes."

41Then Saul said, "O LORD God of Israel, why have You not answered Your servant today? Is the guilt in me or in Jonathan my son? O LORD God of Israel, give Urim. But if it is in Your people Israel, give Thummim." Jonathan and Saul were taken, and the people went free.

42Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and Jonathan my son. Whomever the LORD takes shall die." The people said to Saul, "This shall not be." But Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast the lot between him and Jonathan his son, and Jonathan was taken.

43Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." Jonathan told him, "I tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am; I must die."

44Saul said, "May God do so, and more also; you shall die, Jonathan."

45But the people said to Saul, "Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great deliverance in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has worked with God this day." So the people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.

46Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

Saul's Wars and Household

47When Saul had taken the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab, against the sons of Ammon, against Edom, against the kings of Zobah and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he punished them.

48He acted valiantly and struck Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered them.

49The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi and Malchi-shua. The names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger Michal.

50The name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.

51Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.

52The war against the Philistines was hard all the days of Saul. Whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any man of valor, he took him into his service.

Notes

  • v3 "Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli" — the house of Eli, condemned in 2:30–36, still has a priest, and he stands beside Saul wearing the ephod. Ichabod was born on the day the ark was taken (4:19–21).

  • v6 "nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few" — Gideon's army was cut down because it was too many, or Israel will boast against Me (Judges 7:2). Jonathan goes with one man. His perhaps leaves the outcome to the LORD, and the sign of vv9–10 lets the Philistines' own words decide.

  • v14 "within about half a furrow's length in an acre of field" — ke-vachatsi ma'anah tsemed sadeh, as in half a furrow of a yoke of field. Tsemed is a yoke of oxen, and as a measure the land a yoke plows, as in ten yokes of vineyard (Isaiah 5:10). The twenty fell in a small space. The Greek has with darts and with stones of the field.

  • v15 "it became a trembling from God" — chardat Elohim. In 13:7 Israel followed Saul trembling, charedu; now the trembling is in the Philistine camp, the ground shakes with it, and it is sent by God.

  • v18 "Bring the ephod here… for he carried the ephod on that day before Israel" — these words are in the Greek. The Hebrew has Bring the ark of God here, for the ark of God was on that day, and the sons of Israel, a sentence without an end. The ark was at Kiriath-jearim in the house of Abinadab (7:1–2), where David finds it (2 Samuel 6:3). Ahijah is wearing the ephod (v3), and withdraw your hand (v19) stops the priest in the middle of asking by it. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv24–29 "Saul had put the people under an oath… My father has brought trouble on the land" — akhar, the word Joshua spoke to Achan, Why have you brought trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today (Joshua 7:25). Achan broke the LORD's ban; Saul laid an oath of his own, and his son broke it without knowing. The Greek of v24 opens with Saul committed a great error that day. In v27 the written text has his eyes saw, and the reading is his eyes brightened, which Jonathan repeats in v29, oru einai.

  • vv32–35 "the people ate them with the blood… You have dealt faithlessly" — al ha-dam, the words of the law, You shall not eat anything with the blood in it (Leviticus 19:26). For begadtem, you have dealt faithlessly, the Greek has In Gittaim. The altar of v35 is Saul's first.

  • vv41–42 "give Urim… give Thummim… Whomever the LORD takes shall die" — these words are in the Greek, which names the two lots dēloi, clear ones, its word for Urim again in 28:6, and hosiotēs, holiness. The Hebrew of v41 has only Saul said to the LORD God of Israel, "Give perfect," tamim, from the root of Thummim; LORD God of Israel stands twice in the Greek, and the Hebrew has passed from the first to the second. In v42 the Hebrew passes likewise from between me and Jonathan my son to Jonathan was taken, without the people's protest. The second half of the prayer is compressed even in the Greek, and if it says this, give to Your people Israel, give Thummim. The text follows the Greek.

  • v45 "he has worked with God this day… the people ransomed Jonathan" — im Elohim, with God. The Greek has the people of God, reading the same letters, am, as people. Va-yifdu, ransomed, is the word for redeeming a firstborn son (Exodus 13:13); the Greek has the people prayed for Jonathan.

  • v47 "When Saul had taken the kingship… Wherever he turned, he punished them" — lakhad, the verb of the lot: Saul was taken at Mizpah (10:21), and Jonathan was taken in v42. Yarshia', he declared guilty, punished; the Greek has he was saved.

chapters.title: Saul Rejected
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 15

The Command Against Amalek

1Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people, over Israel. Now then, listen to the words of the LORD.

2Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken note of what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.

3Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that he has. Do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"

4Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.

5Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

6Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, turn aside, go down from among the Amalekites, in case I sweep you away with them. For you showed loyal love to all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt." So the Kenites turned aside from among the Amalekites.

7Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as you come to Shur, which faces Egypt.

8He took Agag king of Amalek alive, and all the people he devoted to destruction with the edge of the sword.

9But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle, the next best and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not devote them to destruction. Everything that was despised and worthless they devoted to destruction.

The LORD Is Sorry

10The word of the LORD came to Samuel:

11"I am sorry that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me and has not carried out My words." Samuel was angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.

12Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning. Samuel was told, "Saul came to Carmel and set up a monument for himself there, and he has turned and passed on and gone down to Gilgal."

13Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you by the LORD! I have carried out the word of the LORD."

14Samuel said, "Then what is this bleating of sheep in my ears, and the lowing of cattle that I hear?"

15Saul said, "They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God. The rest we have devoted to destruction."

16Samuel said to Saul, "Stop, and let me tell you what the LORD said to me tonight." He said to him, "Speak."

17Samuel said, "Though you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.

18The LORD sent you on a mission and said, 'Go, devote to destruction the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until you have wiped them out.'

19Why then did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but pounced on the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?"

20Saul said to Samuel, "But I did listen to the voice of the LORD. I went on the mission on which the LORD sent me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I devoted Amalek to destruction.

21But the people took sheep and cattle from the spoil, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal."

22Samuel said,
"Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices
as much as in listening to the voice of the LORD?
To listen is better than sacrifice,
to pay attention than the fat of rams.

23For rebellion is the sin of soothsaying,
and insistence is wickedness and household gods.
Because you have rejected the word of the LORD,
He has rejected you from being king."

The Torn Robe

24Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.

25Now then, please forgive my sin and return with me, so that I may bow down to the LORD."

26Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."

27As Samuel turned to go, Saul took hold of the edge of his robe, and it tore.

28Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is better than you.

29Also the Enduring One of Israel will not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind."

30Saul said, "I have sinned. Yet honor me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, so that I may bow down to the LORD your God."

31So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.

Agag

32Samuel said, "Bring Agag king of Amalek to me." Agag came to him cheerfully, and Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death has passed."

33Samuel said,
"As your sword has made women childless,
so shall your mother be childless among women."
Samuel hewed Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

34Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.

35Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. The LORD was sorry that He had made Saul king over Israel.

Notes

  • v2 "what Amalek did to Israel… on the way when he came up from Egypt" — Amalek attacked Israel at Rephidim, and the LORD said, I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens (Exodus 17:14). The law repeats it: Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt… you shall blot out the memory of Amalek (Deuteronomy 25:17–19). Samuel gives Saul that command.

  • v3 "devote to destruction" — ve-hacharamtem, the cherem of Jericho, where Israel devoted to destruction all that was in the city, man and woman… ox and sheep and donkey (Joshua 6:21). What is devoted belongs to the LORD, and no one may keep it; that is the point on which Saul fails.

  • v6 "you showed loyal love to all the sons of Israel" — chesed. The Kenites were the family of Moses' father-in-law, who went up with Judah into the land (Judges 1:16). Saul keeps faith with them before he strikes Amalek.

  • v9 "the next best and the lambs" — ha-mishnim, the second ones, as the Levites of the second rank (1 Chronicles 15:18). The Greek has the foods, and for karim, lambs, it has vineyards. Would not, lo avu: the sparing was chosen.

  • vv11, 29, 35 "I am sorry… He is not a man, that He should change His mind… The LORD was sorry" — one verb, nicham, three times. The LORD was sorry over Saul as He was over humankind before the flood (Genesis 6:6). Between the two, v29 says He will not change His mind, close to Balaam's oracle, God is not a man… that He should change His mind (Numbers 23:19): the word just spoken, that the kingdom is torn from Saul (v28), stands. Netsach, the Enduring One, is the word in la-netsach, forever (2 Samuel 2:26). The Greek of v29 has Israel will be divided in two.

  • v12 "set up a monument for himself" — matsiv lo yad, setting up a hand for himself. Yad, hand, is a monument, as Absalom's pillar was called Absalom's hand (2 Samuel 18:18). The Greek goes on in v13 with Saul offering a burnt offering to the Lord, the first of the spoils he had brought from Amalek.

  • v19 "pounced on the spoil" — va-ta'at, the word of 14:32, when the people pounced on the spoil and ate with the blood. In chapter 14 Saul stopped the people from eating with the blood; here the same rush is charged to him.

  • vv22–23 "To listen is better than sacrifice… rebellion is the sin of soothsaying" — shemoa, to listen, is the verb of listen to the words of the LORD (v1) and of Saul's I listened to their voice (v24). Qesem is the practice of the qosem, the soothsayer the law forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10). Haftsar, insistence, is the verb of Lot, who pressed them greatly (Genesis 19:3). The Greek has omen-taking for soothsaying.

  • vv27–28 "Saul took hold of the edge of his robe, and it tore… The LORD has torn the kingdom" — the Hebrew says only he took hold; the Greek names Saul. His robe is Samuel's, since Samuel is the one turning to go: the me'il, the garment his mother made him each year (2:19), and the robe in which Saul will know him at Endor (28:14). David will cut off the edge of Saul's robe (24:4), and Samuel will say again, the LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David (28:17).

  • vv32–33 "Agag came to him cheerfully… Samuel hewed Agag to pieces" — ma'adannot, a form of the word in a king's delicacies (Genesis 49:20), fits Agag's surely the bitterness of death has passed. The same word is the bonds of the Pleiades in Job 38:31, which would put Agag in chains. The Greek has trembling. Va-yeshassef, hewed to pieces, occurs only here.

speech.text: 1 Samuel 15
The Command Against Amalek
Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people, over Israel. Now then, listen to the words of the LORD.
Thus says the LORD of hosts: 'I have taken note of what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
Now go and strike Amalek, and devote to destruction all that he has. Do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"
Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.
Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, turn aside, go down from among the Amalekites, in case I sweep you away with them. For you showed loyal love to all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt." So the Kenites turned aside from among the Amalekites.
Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as you come to Shur, which faces Egypt.
He took Agag king of Amalek alive, and all the people he devoted to destruction with the edge of the sword.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and the cattle, the next best and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not devote them to destruction. Everything that was despised and worthless they devoted to destruction.
The LORD Is Sorry
The word of the LORD came to Samuel:
"I am sorry that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me and has not carried out My words." Samuel was angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning. Samuel was told, "Saul came to Carmel and set up a monument for himself there, and he has turned and passed on and gone down to Gilgal."
Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, "Blessed are you by the LORD! I have carried out the word of the LORD."
Samuel said, "Then what is this bleating of sheep in my ears, and the lowing of cattle that I hear?"
Saul said, "They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God. The rest we have devoted to destruction."
Samuel said to Saul, "Stop, and let me tell you what the LORD said to me tonight." He said to him, "Speak."
Samuel said, "Though you are small in your own eyes, are you not the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.
The LORD sent you on a mission and said, 'Go, devote to destruction the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until you have wiped them out.'
Why then did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but pounced on the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?"
Saul said to Samuel, "But I did listen to the voice of the LORD. I went on the mission on which the LORD sent me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I devoted Amalek to destruction.
But the people took sheep and cattle from the spoil, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal."
Samuel said, "Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in listening to the voice of the LORD? To listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.
For rebellion is the sin of soothsaying, and insistence is wickedness and household gods. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you from being king."
The Torn Robe
Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, for I have transgressed the command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
Now then, please forgive my sin and return with me, so that I may bow down to the LORD."
Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel."
As Samuel turned to go, Saul took hold of the edge of his robe, and it tore.
Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is better than you.
Also the Enduring One of Israel will not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind."
Saul said, "I have sinned. Yet honor me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, so that I may bow down to the LORD your God."
So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.
Agag
Samuel said, "Bring Agag king of Amalek to me." Agag came to him cheerfully, and Agag said, "Surely the bitterness of death has passed."
Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women." Samuel hewed Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel mourned over Saul. The LORD was sorry that He had made Saul king over Israel.

chapters.title: David Anointed
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 16

Samuel at Bethlehem

1The LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have seen among his sons a king for Myself."

2Samuel said, "How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me." The LORD said, "Take a heifer with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'

3Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will let you know what you shall do. You shall anoint for Me the one I name to you."

4Samuel did what the LORD said and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the town came trembling to meet him and said, "Do you come in peace?"

5He said, "In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." He consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

6And it came to pass, when they came, that he saw Eliab and said, "Surely the LORD's anointed stands before Him."

7But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For it is not as a man sees: a man looks at what is before the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart."

8Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. He said, "The LORD has not chosen this one either."

9Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. He said, "The LORD has not chosen this one either."

10Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."

11Samuel said to Jesse, "Are these all the young men?" He said, "There is still the youngest, and he is tending the sheep." Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will not sit down to eat until he comes here."

12So he sent and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look at. The LORD said, "Arise, anoint him, for this is the one."

13Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed on David from that day forward. Then Samuel arose and went to Ramah.

David in Saul's Service

14The Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him.

15Saul's servants said to him, "An evil spirit from God is terrifying you.

16Let our lord command your servants who are before you to look for a man who knows how to play the lyre. And it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is on you, that he will play with his hand, and you will be well."

17Saul said to his servants, "Find me a man who plays well, and bring him to me."

18One of the young men answered, "I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play, a man of worth and a man of war, wise in speech and handsome, and the LORD is with him."

19So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who is with the sheep."

20Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent them by David his son to Saul.

21David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.

22Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my eyes."

23And it would come to pass, whenever the spirit from God was on Saul, that David would take the lyre and play with his hand, and Saul would find relief and be well, and the evil spirit would depart from him.

Notes

  • v1 "I have seen among his sons a king for Myself" — ra'iti… li melekh. Ra'ah, to see, is also to see to, provide, as in God will see to the lamb (Genesis 22:8). The chapter turns on the verb: Samuel saw Eliab (v6), a man sees… the LORD looks (v7), find me, literally see for me (v17), and I have seen a son of Jesse (v18). The first king was the people's request (8:5); this one the LORD has seen for Himself.

  • v4 "The elders of the town came trembling… Do you come in peace?" — va-yecherdu, the trembling of 14:15. A visit from the prophet who had just hewn Agag to pieces (15:33) is not assumed to be peaceful.

  • v7 "the height of his stature… a man looks at what is before the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart" — Saul was chosen taller than any of the people (9:2, 10:23); Eliab is rejected for the same look. The Hebrew is man sees to the eyes, and the LORD sees to the heart. The first half is compressed, for not what a man sees; the Greek supplies God sees.

  • v11 "the youngest… tending the sheep" — ha-qatan, the small one, as Saul was small in your own eyes (15:17). Ro'eh, shepherding, is the word of the LORD's charge to David when he becomes king: You shall shepherd My people Israel (2 Samuel 5:2).

  • v12 "He was ruddy" — admoni, the word used of Esau at his birth, the first came out ruddy (Genesis 25:25). With beautiful eyes, and good to look at: after v7, the narrator still notes the look of the chosen one.

  • vv13–14 "the Spirit of the LORD rushed on David… The Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul" — va-titslach, the word of the Spirit on Saul (10:6, 10:10, 11:6). On David it comes from that day forward, and in the next verse it leaves Saul.

  • v14 "an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him" — as God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem (Judges 9:23). Bi'atattu, terrified him; the Greek has choked him. In v23 the Hebrew calls it only the spirit of God, and names it the evil spirit at the end of the verse; the Greek has evil spirit in both places.

  • v18 "a man of worth and a man of war, wise in speech" — gibbor chayil, as Kish is described (9:1). The servant's picture of David goes past what a musician needs, and ends with the words the story will keep repeating: the LORD is with him (18:12, 18:14, 18:28).

  • v20 "a donkey loaded with bread" — chamor lechem, a donkey of bread. The Greek has a homer of bread, chomer, the same letters read as a measure.

  • vv21, 23 "Saul loved him greatly… Saul would find relief" — Saul is the first to love David; Jonathan (18:1, 18:3), all Israel and Judah (18:16) and Michal (18:20) follow. Ravach, to find relief, have room to breathe, is built on the same letters as ruach, spirit, breath: when the spirit comes on Saul, the music gives him breath.

chapters.title: David and Goliath
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 17

The Champion of Gath

1The Philistines gathered their armies for battle. They gathered at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

2Saul and the men of Israel gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah, and drew up in battle lines to meet the Philistines.

3The Philistines stood on the mountain on one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.

4A champion came out from the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath. His height was six cubits and a span.

5He had a bronze helmet on his head, and he wore a coat of scale armor; the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.

6He had bronze greaves on his legs, and a bronze javelin slung between his shoulders.

7The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the head of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield-bearer went before him.

8He stood and called out to the ranks of Israel, "Why have you come out to draw up for battle? Am I not the Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

9If he is able to fight with me and kills me, we will be your slaves. But if I prevail against him and kill him, you shall be our slaves and serve us."

10The Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together."

11When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they lost heart and were greatly afraid.

David Comes to the Camp

12David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and in the days of Saul the man was old, well on in years.

13The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

14David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,

15but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

16For forty days the Philistine came forward morning and evening and took his stand.

17Jesse said to David his son, "Take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves, and hurry to the camp to your brothers.

18Take these ten cheeses to the commander of their thousand. See how your brothers are, and bring back some token from them.

19Saul and they and all the men of Israel are in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines."

20David rose early in the morning, left the sheep with a keeper, took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, shouting the war cry.

21Israel and the Philistines drew up, line facing line.

22David left his baggage in the care of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the battle line, and came and asked his brothers how they were.

23As he was speaking with them, the champion, Goliath the Philistine of Gath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines and spoke the same words as before, and David heard.

24All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

25The men of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who is coming up? He comes up to defy Israel. The man who kills him, the king will make very rich; he will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel."

26David said to the men standing with him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God?"

27The people answered him in the same way: "So shall it be done for the man who kills him."

28Eliab his oldest brother heard him speaking to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David. He said, "Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your insolence and the evil of your heart; you have come down to see the battle."

29David said, "What have I done now? Was it not only a word?"

30He turned from him to another and spoke the same way, and the people answered him as before.

31When the words David had spoken were heard, they reported them to Saul, and he sent for him.

"The Battle Is the LORD's"

32David said to Saul, "Let no one's heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."

33Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth."

34David said to Saul, "Your servant used to tend his father's sheep. When a lion came, or a bear, and took a lamb from the flock,

35I went out after it and struck it and rescued the lamb from its mouth. If it rose against me, I caught it by its beard, struck it and killed it.

36Your servant has struck down both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, for he has defied the ranks of the living God."

37David said, "The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go, and the LORD be with you."

38Saul clothed David in his own garments. He put a bronze helmet on his head and clothed him in a coat of mail.

39David fastened Saul's sword over the garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. David said to Saul, "I cannot walk in these, for I have not tested them." So David took them off.

40He took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones from the stream, and put them in the shepherd's bag he had, in the pouch. With his sling in his hand, he drew near to the Philistine.

41The Philistine came on, drawing near to David, with the shield-bearer before him.

42When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him, for he was a youth, ruddy and handsome in appearance.

43The Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" Then the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

44The Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field."

45David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.

46This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head. I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and the wild animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,

47and all this assembly may know that the LORD does not save by sword and spear. For the battle is the LORD's, and He will give you into our hand."

48When the Philistine rose and came on and drew near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.

49David put his hand into the bag, took out a stone, slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

50So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in David's hand.

51David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

52The men of Israel and Judah rose with a shout and pursued the Philistines as far as the approach to the valley and to the gates of Ekron. The Philistine dead fell on the road from Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.

53The sons of Israel came back from chasing the Philistines and plundered their camp.

54David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent.

"Whose Son Is This Youth?"

55When Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is this youth?" Abner said, "As your soul lives, O king, I do not know."

56The king said, "Find out whose son the young man is."

57When David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the Philistine's head in his hand.

58Saul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" David said, "The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

Notes

  • v4 "A champion… six cubits and a span" — ish ha-benayim, the man of the space between: the one who steps into the ground between the two lines to fight for his side. The Greek has four cubits and a span.

  • vv5–7 "a coat of scale armor… bronze greaves… like a weaver's beam" — qasqassim, the word for the scales of a fish (Leviticus 11:9). The greaves, mitschat, are built on metsach, forehead: he wears a forehead-piece on his legs, and the stone finds the forehead (v49). A weaver's beam is said again of the spear of Goliath the Gittite in 2 Samuel 21:19, where Elhanan of Bethlehem kills him; 1 Chronicles 20:5 has Elhanan kill Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, with the same spear.

  • vv10, 26 "I defy the ranks of Israel… takes away the disgrace from Israel" — cheraf, defy, taunt, and its noun cherpah, disgrace, the word of Nahash, who wanted to bring disgrace on all Israel (11:2). David hears the taunt as aimed at the ranks of the living God.

  • vv12–31 "David was the son of that Ephrathite" — the Greek has none of vv12–31, nor v41, v50 or vv55–58. Without them, David is already Saul's armor-bearer (16:21) and simply goes out against the Philistine. With them, he is introduced a second time, as a shepherd who brings food to his brothers. The Hebrew keeps both, and the text follows it.

  • v12 "the man was old, well on in years" — the Hebrew is ba va-anashim, come among men. The usual phrase is ba ba-yamim, coming on in days, said of Abraham (Genesis 24:1); the sense is the same.

  • v28 "I know your insolence and the evil of your heart" — Eliab is the brother the LORD passed over with the LORD looks at the heart (16:7). Now Eliab claims to see his youngest brother's heart.

  • vv34–37 "the paw of the lion… the hand of this Philistine" — yad, hand, in both places: David puts the Philistine among the beasts he has already fought (v36). Saul's the LORD be with you echoes the servant's word about David, the LORD is with him (16:18).

  • vv45–47 "the LORD does not save by sword and spear" — in Saul's army neither sword nor spear was found except with Saul and Jonathan (13:22). David turns the lack into the point, as Jonathan did: nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few (14:6). The fight is fought so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.

  • v54 "brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent" — Jerusalem was still held by the Jebusites; David takes it as king (2 Samuel 5:6–9). The sword turns up later with the priest at Nob, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod (21:9).

  • vv55–58 "Whose son is this youth?" — Saul already loved him greatly and made him his armor-bearer (16:21), and sent to Jesse by name (16:22). Here neither Saul nor Abner knows him. This scene is one of those the Greek does not have.

If he is able to fight with me and kills me, we will be your slaves. But if I prevail against him and kill him, you shall be our slaves and serve us."
The Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together."
When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they lost heart and were greatly afraid.
David Comes to the Camp
David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and in the days of Saul the man was old, well on in years.
The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle. The names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
David was the youngest. The three oldest followed Saul,
but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
For forty days the Philistine came forward morning and evening and took his stand.
Jesse said to David his son, "Take for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves, and hurry to the camp to your brothers.
Take these ten cheeses to the commander of their thousand. See how your brothers are, and bring back some token from them.
Saul and they and all the men of Israel are in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines."

David rose early in the morning, left the sheep with a keeper, took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, shouting the war cry.
Israel and the Philistines drew up, line facing line.
David left his baggage in the care of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the battle line, and came and asked his brothers how they were.
As he was speaking with them, the champion, Goliath the Philistine of Gath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines and spoke the same words as before, and David heard.
All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

The men of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who is coming up? He comes up to defy Israel. The man who kills him, the king will make very rich; he will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel."

David said to the men standing with him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God?"
The people answered him in the same way: "So shall it be done for the man who kills him."

Eliab his oldest brother heard him speaking to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David. He said, "Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your insolence and the evil of your heart; you have come down to see the battle."
David said, "What have I done now? Was it not only a word?"
He turned from him to another and spoke the same way, and the people answered him as before.
When the words David had spoken were heard, they reported them to Saul, and he sent for him.
"The Battle Is the LORD's"
David said to Saul, "Let no one's heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."
Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you are a youth, and he has been a man of war from his youth."
David said to Saul, "Your servant used to tend his father's sheep. When a lion came, or a bear, and took a lamb from the flock,
I went out after it and struck it and rescued the lamb from its mouth. If it rose against me, I caught it by its beard, struck it and killed it.
Your servant has struck down both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them, for he has defied the ranks of the living God."
David said, "The LORD who rescued me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, He will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go, and the LORD be with you."
Saul clothed David in his own garments. He put a bronze helmet on his head and clothed him in a coat of mail.
David fastened Saul's sword over the garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested them. David said to Saul, "I cannot walk in these, for I have not tested them." So David took them off.
He took his staff in his hand and chose five smooth stones from the stream, and put them in the shepherd's bag he had, in the pouch. With his sling in his hand, he drew near to the Philistine.
The Philistine came on, drawing near to David, with the shield-bearer before him.
When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him, for he was a youth, ruddy and handsome in appearance.
The Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" Then the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
The Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the field."
David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.

This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head. I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and the wild animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,
and all this assembly may know that the LORD does not save by sword and spear. For the battle is the LORD's, and He will give you into our hand."
When the Philistine rose and came on and drew near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.
David put his hand into the bag, took out a stone, slung it and struck the Philistine on his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in David's hand.
David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

The men of Israel and Judah rose with a shout and pursued the Philistines as far as the approach to the valley and to the gates of Ekron. The Philistine dead fell on the road from Shaaraim as far as Gath and Ekron.
The sons of Israel came back from chasing the Philistines and plundered their camp.
David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent.
"Whose Son Is This Youth?"
When Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is this youth?" Abner said, "As your soul lives, O king, I do not know."
The king said, "Find out whose son the young man is."
When David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the Philistine's head in his hand.
Saul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" David said, "The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

chapters.title: Saul's Jealousy
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 18

Jonathan's Covenant

1And it came to pass, when he had finished speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

2Saul took him that day and would not let him go back to his father's house.

3Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own soul.

4Jonathan stripped off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, and his garments too, even his sword, his bow and his belt.

5David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he succeeded. Saul set him over the men of war, and it was good in the eyes of all the people, and in the eyes of Saul's servants too.

Thousands and Ten Thousands

6And it came to pass, as they were coming, when David returned from killing the Philistine, that the women came out of all the towns of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul, with tambourines, with joy and with cymbals.

7The women sang to one another as they celebrated:
"Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his ten thousands."

8Saul was very angry, and this saying was evil in his eyes. He said, "They have given David ten thousands, and to me they have given thousands. What more can he have but the kingdom?"

9Saul kept his eye on David from that day on.

10And it came to pass the next day that an evil spirit from God rushed on Saul, and he prophesied inside the house while David was playing with his hand, as he did day by day. Saul had the spear in his hand.

11Saul hurled the spear, thinking, "I will pin David to the wall." But David evaded him twice.

12Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him and had departed from Saul.

13So Saul removed him from his presence and made him commander of a thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.

14David succeeded in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.

15When Saul saw that he was succeeding greatly, he stood in dread of him.

16But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.

Saul's Daughters

17Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you as a wife; only be a man of valor for me and fight the LORD's battles." For Saul thought, "Let my hand not be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him."

18David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my life, or my father's clan in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?"

19And it came to pass, at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, that she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.

20Michal, Saul's daughter, loved David. They told Saul, and the thing was right in his eyes.

21Saul thought, "I will give her to him, so that she may be a snare to him, and so that the hand of the Philistines may be against him." So Saul said to David, "Through the second you shall become my son-in-law today."

22Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David in secret and say, 'The king delights in you, and all his servants love you. And now become the king's son-in-law.'"

23Saul's servants spoke these words in David's hearing. David said, "Is it a light thing in your eyes to become the king's son-in-law, when I am a poor man and lightly esteemed?"

24Saul's servants told him, "These are the words David spoke."

25Saul said, "Say this to David: 'The king desires no bride-price except a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance on the king's enemies.'" For Saul planned to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

26When his servants told David these words, the thing was right in David's eyes, to become the king's son-in-law. Before the days were fulfilled,

27David arose and went, he and his men, and struck down two hundred men of the Philistines. David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, so that he might become the king's son-in-law. So Saul gave him Michal his daughter as a wife.

28Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, Saul's daughter, loved him.

29Saul was still more afraid of David, and Saul was David's enemy all his days.

30The commanders of the Philistines came out to battle, and as often as they came out, David succeeded more than all Saul's servants, so that his name was held in high honor.

Notes

  • v1 "the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David" — nefesh… niqsherah be-nefesh, the words Judah used of Jacob and Benjamin: his life is bound up with the boy's life (Genesis 44:30). As his own soul, ke-nafsho, comes twice (vv1, 3).

  • vv1–5 and the Greek — the Greek has none of vv1–5, vv10–11, vv17–19 or v30, and it lacks the end of vv21, 26 and 29. Without them there is no covenant with Jonathan here, no spear thrown, and no offer of Merab. The Hebrew has them, and the text follows it.

  • v4 "the robe he was wearing… even his sword, his bow and his belt" — me'il, the robe. When the Philistines kept the smiths, neither sword nor spear was found in Israel except with Saul and Jonathan (13:22). David could not walk in Saul's armor (17:39); Jonathan gives him his own sword.

  • vv5, 14, 15, 30 "he succeeded" — maskil, acting wisely, succeeding: the word joins good sense and good outcome. It comes four times in the chapter, and Saul's fear grows beside it (vv12, 15, 29).

  • v6 "with tambourines, with joy and with cymbals" — shalishim, an instrument built on shalosh, three; what it was is not known. The Greek has cymbals, and the text follows it. The Greek also has the women come out to meet David, not King Saul.

  • v7 "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands" — thousands and ten thousands stand as a pair in Hebrew poetry: How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight (Deuteronomy 32:30). Saul hears the pair as a ranking (v8). The song follows David: the servants of Achish quote it at Gath (21:11), and the Philistine commanders quote it again (29:5).

  • v10 "an evil spirit from God rushed on Saul, and he prophesied" — va-titslach, the verb of the Spirit of God on Saul at his anointing (10:6, 10:10), and on David (16:13). Va-yitnabbe, he prophesied, is the word of 10:10 too; what came on him then from the Spirit of God now comes from an evil spirit.

  • vv17, 21, 25 "let the hand of the Philistines be against him… a snare to him" — three times Saul's plan is given in his own mind. Moqesh, snare, is the word Israel was warned about in the land (Judges 2:3).

  • v18 "Who am I… that I should be son-in-law to the king?" — Moses' question at the bush, Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh? (Exodus 3:11).

  • vv25, 27 "a hundred foreskins… two hundred men" — mohar, the bride-price that Shechem offered to raise as high as Jacob's sons liked (Genesis 34:12). David pays double. The Greek has a hundred in v27, and David names the price later as a hundred foreskins of the Philistines (2 Samuel 3:14).

chapters.title: David Escapes
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 19

Jonathan Speaks for David

1Saul told Jonathan his son and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted greatly in David.

2Jonathan told David, "Saul my father is seeking to kill you. So now, please, be on your guard in the morning; stay in a secret place and hide.

3I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father. If I see anything, I will tell you."

4Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father. He said to him, "Let the king not sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds have been very good for you.

5He took his life in his hand and struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then would you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?"

6Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, "As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death."

7Jonathan called David and told him all these words. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.

Michal Saves David

8There was war again. David went out and fought the Philistines and struck them with a great slaughter, and they fled before him.

9Then an evil spirit from the LORD came on Saul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand, while David was playing with his hand.

10Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slipped away from Saul, and Saul drove the spear into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.

11Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him, "If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death."

12So Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped.

13Michal took the household gods and laid them in the bed, put a net of goats' hair at the head, and covered it with the garment.

14When Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, "He is sick."

15Then Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me in the bed, so that I may kill him."

16When the messengers came in, there were the household gods in the bed, with the net of goats' hair at the head.

17Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?" Michal answered Saul, "He said to me, 'Let me go. Why should I kill you?'"

Saul Among the Prophets

18David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. He and Samuel went and stayed at Naioth.

19Saul was told, "David is at Naioth in Ramah."

20Saul sent messengers to take David. When they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing as leader over them, the Spirit of God came on Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.

21When Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they also prophesied.

22Then he himself went to Ramah and came to the great cistern that is in Secu. He asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" Someone said, "They are at Naioth in Ramah."

23So he went there, to Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of God came on him too, and he went along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.

24He too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Samuel, and he lay naked all that day and all that night. That is why they say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

Notes

  • v1 "Jonathan… delighted greatly in David" — chafets, the word Saul's servants were told to use to lure David, the king delights in you (18:22). The king's delight was a trap; his son's is real.

  • v5 "He took his life in his hand… without cause" — sam nafsho be-khappo, as Jephthah said, I took my life in my hands (Judges 12:3). Chinnam, for nothing, without cause: Jonathan lays the case before his father like a judge, and Saul yields to it with an oath (v6).

  • vv9–10 "an evil spirit from the LORD… Saul drove the spear into the wall" — in 18:11 David evaded the spear twice; now Saul throws it again. The oath of v6 lasts until the next victory over the Philistines (v8).

  • v12 "Michal let David down through the window" — the rescue of the spies at Jericho: she let them down by a rope through the window (Joshua 2:15). The king's daughter takes the part Rahab took against her own king.

  • vv13–17 "Michal took the household gods… Why have you deceived me like this?" — terafim, the household gods Rachel stole from her father Laban and hid by sitting on them, telling him she could not rise (Genesis 31:34–35). Michal too hides the husband her father hunts, with household gods, and answers her father with a lie. Kevir, net or quilt of goats' hair, occurs only in vv13 and 16. The Greek has the liver of goats.

  • vv18–23 "Naioth in Ramah" — Nayot is named only in this chapter and in 20:1. The Greek has Auath.

  • v20 "the company of the prophets" — lahaqat, which occurs only here. The Greek has the assembly; qehillah, assembly, has the same letters as lahaqah in another order.

  • vv20–23 "the Spirit of God came on Saul's messengers… on him too" — three sets of messengers, then the king himself, are stopped by the Spirit before they can reach David. At his anointing the Spirit made Saul another man (10:6); now it comes on him while he hunts David.

  • v24 "He too stripped off his clothes… before Samuel" — va-yifshat, the verb of Jonathan, who stripped off the robe and gave it to David (18:4). Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death (15:35) speaks of Samuel going to Saul; here Saul comes before Samuel.

  • v24 "Is Saul also among the prophets?" — the proverb's second origin. At 10:11–12 it began with Saul newly anointed and prophesying among the prophets; here it is said of a king lying naked on the ground.

chapters.title: Jonathan's Arrows
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 20

David and Jonathan

1David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and said to Jonathan, "What have I done? What is my guilt, and what is my sin against your father, that he is seeking my life?"

2He said to him, "Far from it! You shall not die. My father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. Why should my father hide this from me? It is not so."

3But David swore again and said, "Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he thinks, 'Let Jonathan not know this, or he will be grieved.' But truly, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is only a step between me and death."

4Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul says, I will do for you."

5David said to Jonathan, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and I ought to sit with the king to eat. Let me go, so that I may hide in the field until the evening of the third day.

6If your father misses me at all, say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me to run to Bethlehem, his town, for there is a yearly sacrifice there for the whole clan.'

7If he says, 'Good,' your servant will be safe. But if he burns with anger, know that he has resolved on evil.

8Show loyal love to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. But if there is guilt in me, kill me yourself. Why should you bring me to your father?"

9Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! If I knew for certain that my father had resolved that evil should come on you, would I not tell you?"

10David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?"

11Jonathan said to David, "Come, let us go out into the field." So the two of them went out into the field.

The Covenant Renewed

12Jonathan said to David, "The LORD, the God of Israel, is witness: when I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, if he is well disposed toward David, will I not then send to you and tell you?

13May the LORD do so to Jonathan, and more also, if my father means to do you evil and I do not tell you and send you away, so that you may go in peace. May the LORD be with you, as He has been with my father.

14If I am still alive, will you not show me the loyal love of the LORD, so that I do not die?

15Do not cut off your loyal love from my house forever, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth."

16So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David: "May the LORD require it at the hand of David's enemies."

17Jonathan made David swear again by his love for him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul.

18Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.

35And it came to pass in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field to the meeting with David, and a little boy was with him.

39The boy knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.

40Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, "Go, carry them to the town."

  • vv5, 18, 24 "the new moon" — chodesh, the first day of the month, marked by its own burnt offerings (Numbers 28:11) and by trumpets at the beginnings of your months (Numbers 10:10). The king's household ate together at it, and an empty seat was noticed.

  • v8 "Show loyal love to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD" — chesed, the loyalty owed inside a covenant. The covenant is the one Jonathan made in 18:3; David calls it a covenant of the LORD, made before Him.

  • v13 "May the LORD be with you, as He has been with my father" — the LORD is with him is the story's word for David (16:18, 18:12, 18:14). The king's son says it to David as a blessing, and speaks of the LORD's presence with Saul as past.

  • vv14–15 "show me the loyal love of the LORD… Do not cut off your loyal love from my house" — karat, cut off, runs through the verses: do not cut off your loyal love… when the LORD cuts off David's enemies, and Jonathan cut, made, a covenant (v16). David keeps it when he is king: Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, so that I may show him loyal love for Jonathan's sake? (2 Samuel 9:1), and Jonathan's son shall eat bread at my table always (2 Samuel 9:7), the table David is missing here.

  • v18 "you will be missed, because your seat will be empty" — ve-nifqadta ki yippaqed moshavekha: the same verb, paqad, to be looked for, and so to be missed or empty, is used of David and of his seat.

  • v26 "He is not clean; surely he is not clean" — the new-moon meal was a sacrifice (v29), and the person who eats flesh from the peace offering… while he is unclean is cut off (Leviticus 7:20). Saul supposes an accident has made David unable to come.

  • vv27, 30, 31 "the son of Jesse" — Saul does not say David's name in the chapter. Three times he calls him the son of Jesse.

  • v31 "he deserves to die" — ben mavet, a son of death. David will say it of the rich man in Nathan's story: As the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die (2 Samuel 12:5).

  • v33 "Saul hurled the spear at him" — va-yatel, the verb of the spear at David (18:11). Now Saul throws it at his own son, and Jonathan has his answer to Why should he be put to death? (v32).

  • v42 "Then David rose and went, and Jonathan went into the town" — in the Hebrew these words are 21:1, and the rest of chapter 21 runs one verse ahead of the English. The Greek has them as 20:43.
